title: AI YouTube Intro Generator
summary: Make a YouTube intro with AI. Copy one of 12 free YouTube intro templates for your kind of channel, add your name, and Flick makes the clip.
body_markdown:
### Are these YouTube intro templates free?


Yes, every template here runs on the Flick free plan: you get 100 credits when you sign up, 200 more for joining the Flick Discord, and 100 credits every week. A five-second clip with MiniMax H3 Fast costs 20 credits, and downloads carry a Flick watermark until the Standard plan.


### How long should a YouTube intro be?


Most channels keep an intro to about five seconds or less, so viewers reach the video quickly. Many creators open with a short hook first and show the intro after it.


### How do I make a YouTube intro with my own logo?


Upload your logo to a Flick canvas, set it as the start frame of an image to video clip and describe what moves around it. Tell the model the logo never changes shape, and lock the camera.


### Do YouTube videos need an intro?


No. Many channels skip a long intro and start with the most interesting moment, then use a short branded card as a signature. A brief intro helps most when viewers should recognise your channel from video to video.


### Can I use AI to make a YouTube intro?


Yes. An image model can make a title frame with your channel name lettered on it, and a video model can animate that frame. Read the name carefully in the finished clip, since small or long names are the most likely to warp.


### How do I add an intro to a YouTube video?


Add the intro clip to the start of your project in a video editor, or after your opening hook, then export the finished video and upload it as usual. You can download the clip from Flick for any editor you already use.
